statement.en: This level is set in Québec City, where Champlain built a fortress in 1608. Discover Canada says he allied the colony with the Algonquin, the Montagnais and the Huron, and it calls them historic enemies of the Iroquois. The French and the Iroquois made peace in 1701.
statement.fr: Ce niveau se déroule à Québec, où Champlain a bâti un fort en 1608. Découvrir le Canada dit qu'il a allié la colonie aux Algonquin, aux Montagnais et aux Huron, et les appelle les ennemis historiques des Iroquois. Les Français et les Iroquois ont fait la paix en 1701.

source.quote: allied the colony with the Algonquin, Montagnais, and Huron, historic enemies of the Iroquois

verification.evidence: In 1608 Champlain built a fortress at what is now Québec City. … Champlain allied the colony with the Algonquin, Montagnais, and Huron, historic enemies of the Iroquois, a confederation of five (later six) First Nations who battled with the French settlements for a century. The French and the Iroquois made peace in 1701.

blurb.en: Samuel de Champlain built a fort in 1608 where Québec City stands today.
blurb.fr: Samuel de Champlain a bâti un fort en 1608 à l'endroit où se trouve aujourd'hui la ville de Québec.

source.quote: In 1608 Champlain built a fortress at what is now Québec City.

verification.evidence: In 1604, the first European settlement north of Florida was established by French explorers Pierre de Monts and Samuel de Champlain, first on St. Croix Island (in present-day Maine), then at Port-Royal, in Acadia (present-day Nova Scotia). In 1608 Champlain built a fortress at what is now Québec City.

blurb.en: In 1759 the British defeated the French at the Battle of the Plains of Abraham, here at Québec City. It marked the end of France's empire in America.
blurb.fr: En 1759, les Britanniques ont vaincu les Français à la bataille des plaines d'Abraham, ici à Québec. Cela a marqué la fin de l'empire français en Amérique.

source.quote: In 1759, the British defeated the French in the Battle of the Plains of Abraham at Québec City — marking the end of France's empire in America.

verification.evidence: In 1759, the British defeated the French in the Battle of the Plains of Abraham at Québec City — marking the end of France’s empire in America.

blurb.en: This open bandstand has a striped roof and white posts, and snow lies on the walkway around it. The British paid for a costly set of defences across the country. It included the Citadel here in Québec City, the one at Halifax with its naval drydock, and Fort Henry at Kingston. People visit all of them today.
blurb.fr: Ce kiosque à musique ouvert a un toit rayé et des poteaux blancs, et la neige couvre l'allée tout autour. Les Britanniques ont payé un coûteux ensemble de défenses au pays. On y trouve la citadelle d'ici, à Québec, celle d'Halifax avec sa cale sèche navale, et le fort Henry à Kingston. Ce sont aujourd'hui des lieux que l'on visite.

source.quote: The British paid for a costly Canadian defence system, including the Citadels at Halifax and Québec City, the naval drydock at Halifax and Fort Henry at Kingston—today popular historic sites.

verification.evidence: The British paid for a costly Canadian defence system, including the Citadels at Halifax and Québec City, the naval drydock at Halifax and Fort Henry at Kingston—today popular historic sites.

blurb.en: This monument remembers two men, James Wolfe and the Marquis de Montcalm. Each one was the commander of an army. Both of them died in battle while they led their soldiers.
blurb.fr: Ce monument rappelle le souvenir de deux hommes, James Wolfe et le marquis de Montcalm. Chacun était le commandant d'une armée. Tous les deux sont morts au combat pendant qu'ils menaient leurs soldats.

source.quote: The commanders of both armies, Brigadier James Wolfe and the Marquis de Montcalm, were killed leading their troops in battle.

verification.evidence: The commanders of both armies, Brigadier James Wolfe and the Marquis de Montcalm, were killed leading their troops in battle.

blurb.en: This is Martello Tower 1, on the Plains of Abraham. Under British rule, the French-speaking Catholic people were called habitants or Canadiens. They tried hard to keep their own way of life in an empire that spoke English and was ruled by Protestants.
blurb.fr: Voici la tour Martello 1, sur les plaines d'Abraham. Sous le régime britannique, on appelait habitants ou Canadiens les catholiques de langue française. Ils se sont efforcés de garder leur propre mode de vie dans un empire de langue anglaise dirigé par des protestants.

source.quote: The French-speaking Catholic people, known as habitants or Canadiens, strove to preserve their way of life in the English-speaking, Protestant-ruled British Empire.

verification.evidence: Following the war, Great Britain renamed the colony the “Province of Quebec.” The French-speaking Catholic people, known as habitants or Canadiens, strove to preserve their way of life in the English-speaking, Protestant-ruled British Empire.

blurb.en: This is the Parliament Building in Québec City. In 1791 a law called the Constitutional Act split the Province of Quebec in two. Upper Canada, later Ontario, was mostly Loyalist, Protestant and English-speaking. Lower Canada, later Quebec, was mostly Catholic and French-speaking.
blurb.fr: Voici l'hôtel du Parlement, à Québec. En 1791, une loi appelée l'Acte constitutionnel a divisé la province de Québec en deux. Le Haut-Canada, plus tard l'Ontario, était surtout loyaliste, protestant et de langue anglaise. Le Bas-Canada, plus tard le Québec, était surtout catholique et de langue française.

source.quote: The Constitutional Act of 1791 divided the Province of Quebec into Upper Canada (later Ontario), which was mainly Loyalist, Protestant and English-speaking, and Lower Canada (later Quebec), heavily Catholic and French-speaking.

verification.evidence: The Constitutional Act of 1791 divided the Province of Quebec into Upper Canada (later Ontario), which was mainly Loyalist, Protestant and English-speaking, and Lower Canada (later Quebec), heavily Catholic and French-speaking.
